newsitem.title: CHINA: Women's place not yet in parliament, group finds.
newsitem.headline: Women's place not yet in parliament, group finds.

text.p: Women are still badly under-represented in the world's parliaments, with less than 11 percent of legislators female, an international parliamentary organisation said on Sunday.
The number of women parliamentarians around the world had slipped one percent since 1995, said the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), which opens its 96th international conference in Beijing on Monday.

Women accounted for just over 100 of the nearly 600 members of parliament in Beijing to discuss human rights, food and other matters, a far higher level of participation than the global average of 10.4 percent, the union said in a statement.

"Democracy will only assume true significance when political policies and national legislation are decided upon jointly between men and women in the interests of both halves of the population," it said.

The group said IPU data showed 40.4 percent of legislators in Sweden were female, the highest level of representation, but found that none of the lawmakers in Papua New Guinea, Kuwait or Mauritania were women.
